proof: on a real worktree the review's edit lands as one FileChanged (provenance user_direct_edit, op user_direct_edit:edit, diff by reference, the command id where a tool call id would be) and one UserPatchApplied in one transaction; the workspace revision advances exactly once; GetCodeView bound to the old file revision reads stale; a replayed command id writes nothing; a stale workspace or file revision is refused STALE_REVISION with the file untouched; a symlink resolving to .env and .env itself are refused PROTECTED_PATH; an ambiguous target is NO_UNIQUE_MATCH. Desktop: the review's Edit panel applies at the revision shown, the file on disk is what the Core applied, the panel is empty afterwards and after a reload, a second window's edit makes the first window's stale edit fail STALE_REVISION, a client naming .env through the preload API is refused PROTECTED_PATH.
audit: DOCUMENTED-ONLY before: the file service had the transaction, preconditions and path policy; no command let a person write through it; no user_direct_edit provenance anywhere.
limitations: one text edit per command; the desktop offers the panel for candidate files while the Core's path policy gates any path named through the API; the CLI holds nothing between commands.
